scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance was created by Singo Wulu, a man from Ponorogo who settled in Blimbing village, Klabang district, and served as its first village head.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed annually at the Bersih Desa ritual in Blimbing village and at the Bondowoso anniversary on August 16.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The lion costume is made of raffia string.
Warok dancers wear black with red-white shirts and carry a cemethi, while female dancers wear kebaya and sampur.

narration: Singo Wulu (the creator and first head of Blimbing village), Nyi Moena, and Ki Jasiman.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Singo Ulung is shares music of Barongsai: The dance is visually compared to Barongsai, though the costumes and equipment are simpler.
Singo Ulung is sibling of Sisingaan: Both are Indonesian lion-themed performance traditions.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The dance is a required element of the Bersih Desa ritual ceremony in Blimbing village and is considered a main means that cannot be replaced.

scenes.title: Until next time
narration: Discover the origins of Singo Ulung, a ritual lion dance from Bondowoso that anchors the spiritual life of a Javanese village.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Singo Ulung (Indonesia). Mood: astonishing. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
